content_type_routes.description: Maps each content type class name to the vendor mirrors that receive its rendered output.

content_type_delivery_caps.description: Delivery limit, in bytes, in force for a rendered content type at a vendor. A missing entry means no known limit — never a fabricated one. Codex truncates root AGENTS.md past project_doc_max_bytes (openai/codex#7138). That key is configurable in principle, but gzkit has NO ROUTE TO SET IT (measured 2026-09-04, GHI #962): Codex reads $CODEX_HOME/config.toml and never the project-local .codex/config.toml gzkit generates, writing to ~/.codex/ is an adopter's global surface the operator ruled out, and repointing CODEX_HOME moves auth.json with it. So this entry records the cap ACTUALLY IN FORCE — Codex's own default — never a limit gzkit established. Raising it without a delivery route re-creates the false-headroom reading GHI #962 names. The generated config declares the same number; CodexDocCapCoherenceTest fail-closes on divergence.

content_type_temperatures.description: Per-vendor temperature for each content type. Each key is a content type class name; each value maps vendor name to temperature tier.

surface_content_types.description: Maps each rendered control surface to the content type that owns it — the inverse direction of content_type_routes, and the authority that makes "is this consumer on-route FOR THIS SURFACE" answerable. Without it a route test can only ask whether a consumer is routed for SOMETHING, which grades an off-content-type rendition (GHI #840).
